findings.claim: The Inputs section says `version` takes "X.Y.Z with no v", but release.yml's version input also accepts a pre-release version X.Y.Z{a,b,rc}N. An operator who wants an exact pre-release version would think they cannot type one.

_regenerates lets through any sentence about regenerating that also holds "not", so "If the notes are not complete, regenerate them." passes as a ban. The r3/r4 "never regenerates" check is weaker than it looks. Matching only a ban that comes before the verb (never/do not/don't regenerate, never regenerated) would close it.

verdict.text: The skill is accurate and plain.
It answers both of the operator's questions.
release.yml opens the version pull request, and release-tag.yml tags the merge commit on the later push to main.
release-tag is not an APM workflow, but it watches apm/apm.yml because users pin the APM package to the CLI tag.
Notes are guaranteed because release-tag refuses a missing or blank notes file.
The rule shrank to the two constraints and points at the skill.
Two small non-blocking fixes remain: the version input's format in the skill, and a loose check in the test that looks for advice to regenerate notes.
Ran `loopctl gate stamp` from the worktree.
It passed lint, format, tests, integration and eval rows r1 to r4: "stamp green: c19b70de402217c7a0a829101a3074e42dd3e73fab82bb70ad62d937a430d32a".
Checked every claim in SKILL.md against release.yml and release-tag.yml.

That covered the inputs and their options, the dry-run step summary (it names the notes source), the off-main refusal, the `release/<tag>` branch, the notes committed as `.github/release-notes/<tag>.md` via `mkdir -p`, the PR body holding the notes plus the before-hermes section, the push-path trigger, one matrix job per package with "nothing to release" for the other, the missing-or-blank refusal, the late-commit `::warning::` and the "Commits missing from the <tag> notes" summary heading, and "only kmctl is Latest".
I also checked the cited scripts (release_notes.py, hermes_release_notes.py --before, next_release_version.py, where --version is required with no tag yet).
`gh run list --commit` exists in the installed gh.
Eval rows.
r1's tests check the name, the inputs against the parsed release.yml, the packages against the input's options and the paths, and they include negative tests for a made-up input and a missing path.
r2's two `-k explains` tests check the needed phrases inside the "Why two workflows" section.
r3: `-k rule` selects all of test_rules.py plus the three rule tests, which check both constraints, gh release edit, the committed file, release_notes.py and "never regenerated".
r4: the step 4 and step 5 section tests check the run commands, the warning, both edit targets and the ban on regenerating.
f2 is the only weakness I found.

The builder's open decision on `.github/release-notes/`: the path rule accepts a placeholder folder only when release.yml has `mkdir -p <folder>`, so it is tied to the real workflow and fails if that line goes.
Adding the folder to test_rules' PLANNED is consistent with how `packages/` and `docs/` are handled.
A placeholder file would be worse: it would sit in the folder release-tag reads notes from.
I accept the deviation from the plan's wording.
releases.md: the cited paths exist, and the reworded every-release-has-notes matches the plan's D3 wording.
f1: the skill's `version` bullet leaves out the pre-release form that release.yml's input description allows.
Fix the docs only.
f2: the regenerate check in the test exempts any sentence containing "not".
Tighten it so a ban only counts when it comes before the verb.
